core_obligations: Choose homogeneous generators and obtain the presentation of M by a direct sum of shifted free modules (proof lines 5871-5878).
Write the presentation in each degree and deduce that each graded piece of M is a finite flat, hence free, module over the local ring (proof lines 5879-5886).
Deduce that each graded piece of the kernel is finite flat, hence free, over the local ring (proof lines 5887-5899).

Tensor the degreewise sequences with the residue field, and use Noetherianity of the graded polynomial algebra over the residue field to choose finitely many homogeneous kernel elements generating after tensoring (proof lines 5901-5905).
Apply Nakayama's lemma degree by degree to conclude that the kernel is generated by those elements, so that M is finitely presented (proof lines 5906-5910).
proof_roadmap: Present M by shifted free modules (proof lines 5871-5878).
Show each graded piece of M and of the kernel is finite free over the local ring (proof lines 5879-5899).
Find finitely many kernel generators after tensoring with the residue field (proof lines 5901-5905).
Lift the generating set by Nakayama (proof lines 5906-5910).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a finite graded module over a graded polynomial algebra over a local ring is finitely presented as soon as it is flat over the base ring. The proof chooses homogeneous generators, writes down the resulting presentation by free graded modules, examines it degree by degree, and observes that each graded piece of the module is finite flat, hence free, over the local ring, which makes each graded piece of the kernel finite flat and therefore free. The kernel is then generated by finitely many homogeneous elements: after tensoring the degreewise sequences with the residue field, Noetherianity of the graded polynomial algebra over the residue field provides finitely many homogeneous elements whose images generate, and Nakayama's lemma upgrades that to generation over the base ring.
